Armed men have killed at least 38 civilians in an ambush in western Niger near the borders with Burkina Faso and Mali, local sources said on Friday. The attack targeted residents of the village of Tillim who were heading early on Thursday to a weekly market in the town of Tera in the restive Tillaberi region.
Escorted by members of a local self-defence group, the villagers fell into an ambush by unidentified armed men, a former elected official said. He said 37 people were killed on the spot and another succumbed to their wounds a day later.
The dead included 11 members of the self-defence escort, 20 men and seven women, according to local accounts. A resident of Tera said the attack killed 37 people including women and children, and residents said children were also among the casualties.
The gunmen had not been identified, and no group had claimed the attack in the reporting available on Friday. There was no immediate official statement from Niger's government. One unconfirmed report attributed the attack to the Islamic State in the Greater Sahara, a claim that has not been confirmed by other sources.
Niger's Tillaberi region, on the borders with Mali and Burkina Faso, has become the epicentre of jihadist attacks in the central Sahel. Niger, ruled by a military junta since a 2023 coup, is battling violence by jihadists linked to Al-Qaeda and the Islamic State group.
The Islamic State in the Greater Sahara has been competing for territorial expansion across the Sahel with Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin, an extremist group linked to Al-Qaeda. Both groups have targeted civilians, security forces and local self-defence groups in the tri-border zone.
Last year, Tillaberi became the deadliest region in the central Sahel where civilians were the most targeted, according to the conflict monitor ACLED. The region hosts just under half of the 450,000 people registered as displaced in Niger, according to the United Nations.
The toll from Thursday's ambush rests on local sources and has not been confirmed by officials, so the figures may change as more information reaches Tera. Market convoys in the region routinely travel under escort because of the risk of attack on the roads.
Gunmen ambushed a convoy of villagers from Tillim travelling under escort to a weekly market in Tera, in the Tillaberi region, killing 37 people on the spot. Another victim died of wounds a day later, taking the toll to at least 38.
The dead included 11 self-defence fighters, 20 men and seven women, according to local accounts. Residents said women and children were among the casualties.
The gunmen have not been identified and no group has claimed the attack. One unconfirmed report attributed it to the Islamic State in the Greater Sahara, a claim that has not been confirmed by other sources.
Tillaberi, on Niger's borders with Mali and Burkina Faso, has become the epicentre of jihadist attacks in the central Sahel. Last year it was the deadliest region in the central Sahel for civilians, according to the conflict monitor ACLED.
